Malayalam actor Sangeeth Prathap has shared his admiration for director Karthik Subbaraj 's 'Dorothy', describing it as an unforgettable cinematic experience. In a social media post, the actor revealed that the film left such a strong impression on him that he does not wish to watch it again. He also expressed his belief that nothing could recreate the feeling of experiencing the movie for the first time. Sharing his reaction, Sangeeth Prathap wrote, "I am choosing to never rewatch Dorothy. It gave me the best two and a half hours of my life. And I know nothing will ever compare to the magic of that first time." Watch Keerthy Suresh Turns Heads at Lakmé Fashion Week with Stunning Look 'Dorothy' is directed by Karthik Subbaraj and features Sananth, Rishikanth and Keerthy Suresh in the lead roles. The movie explores friendship, family conditioning and the influence of patriarchy on individuals. Its story follows two childhood friends whose lives take different directions as they grow older. Karthik Subbaraj explores friendship against a patriarchal backdrop
 At its centre, 'Dorothy' follows Subbu and Karthi, two boys raised in an environment where male dominance and violence shape everyday life. Their childhood experiences influence how they understand relationships, morality and the world outside their immediate surroundings. As adults, they begin to develop contrasting personalities and beliefs. The film examines whether their friendship can survive these changes. It also raises questions about empathy and acceptance in a society where rigid family traditions often dictate personal choices. Subbu's family and its rigid beliefs
 Subbu grows up in a household controlled by his father, Whistle Veeraiya (Muthukumar), and his two brothers. The family has no women, and its members follow a violent interpretation of honour and tradition. Honour killings are treated as part of their established way of life. Subbu's early conversations with Karthi reveal how unfamiliar they are with alternative ways of living. Their understanding of right and wrong comes largely from the environment in which they have been raised. The film uses their childhood experiences to establish the social conditioning that later influences their decisions. How the childhood friends change as adults
 As the characters grow older, their personalities begin to move in opposite directions. Karthi (Rishikanth) becomes increasingly hot-headed, resembling the aggressive men in Subbu's family. Subbu, meanwhile, takes on the role of someone who tries to calm conflicts and bring people together. Their changing attitudes create tension in a friendship that once seemed uncomplicated. The story takes another turn when Subbu's brother Velu (Shanmugaraja) brings Dorothy (Keerthy Suresh), a Malayali woman, home as his wife. Her arrival introduces someone with a different background and perspective into the family. For Subbu, Dorothy becomes a person with whom he can share a connection beyond the household's restrictive atmosphere. However, her presence also challenges the family's established beliefs. The movie is presented by the 'Retro' director in a crime drama mixed with romance elements. Karthik Subbaraj's 'Dorothy' received four stars out of five from ETimes. Poll Vote & Share your view
